name: Bi-variate Volume Rendering
definition: A volume rendering model that blends two data sets: a primary scalar data set (e.g., velocity magnitude) defining opacity/region, and a secondary LIC texture data set defining color/texture. Allows interactive tracking of scalar features and vector flow.
summary: Bi-variate volume rendering visualizes vector flow fields by blending a primary scalar dataset for geometry with a secondary LIC texture for color, decoupling opacity from color to reveal flow within volumetric regions.
